pass_a_gloss: Tome 4. [Lemma, Isaiah 58:8-9:] Then your light will break forth early, and your healings will rise quickly, and your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will wrap around you. Then you will cry, and God will listen to you. While you are still speaking he will say: Behold, I am present. If you should fast purely, he says, and show to God hands wiped clean, and a mind freed from every filth, or when you scrub [yourself] off from striking the lowly with fists, and from goading those under hand into judgment and fights, and from following your own [another reading: your] wishes and love of pleasures, when you break the bread for the hungry, clothe the naked, bring roofless poor into your house; then your light will break forth early. The word has very great emphasis. For he did not say simply: The light will be given to you by God, but rather it will break forth, as in the manner of some lightning, being sent down by God with rush and run, through which the eagerness of the supplier is shown clearly. And saying early, he teaches that it will come down even before time. For God, the steward of our affairs, the giver of spiritual gifts, knows, he knows, the time suited to the generosities upon each. But if someone should become fine and good, and besides compassionate and easily reined, to this one also early the gifts from him will be given, so as to rise in him in the manner of ears of grain; and his healings, that is, the casting off of every sickness, and the running in instead of the better things. For when someone is freed from sicknesses of soul, he will wholly bear fruit, the longing and eagerness toward anything whatever of the good things. The divine and spiritual light then having shone through in us, in every way and wholly the healings rise together too, God dressing our wounds and taking the sinews out of the passions, and putting in instead in us the willing to do good, and to be distinguished in righteousness. For this reason he says that, Your righteousness will go before you. And it will go before clearly making easy beforehand the way toward piety, and moving the rough to the smooth and passable, and bringing down the steep, and as it were setting straight the course upon all the best things. And he adds also something else: For the glory of God, he says, will wrap around you, that is, will encircle you, and will set you looked-upon, and a common benefit to many. For the bright[ness] of the saints [the section breaks off mid-word].
pass_b_english: Tomos 4. “Then your light will break forth early, and your healing will spring up quickly; your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will wrap around you. Then you will cry out, and God will hear you; while you are still speaking he will say, ‘Here I am’” (Isaiah 58:8–9).

If you fast purely, he says, and show God hands washed clean and a mind set free from every stain; that is, when you scrub yourself clean of striking the lowly with your fists, of goading those under your hand into lawsuits and quarrels, and of following your own wishes and pleasures (Isaiah 58:3–4); when you break your bread for the hungry, clothe the naked, and bring the homeless poor into your house (Isaiah 58:7): then your light will break forth early.

The word carries very great force. For he did not simply say, “The light will be given to you by God,” but rather “it will break forth,” like a flash of lightning sent down from God with rush and speed. This clearly shows the eagerness of the Giver. And by saying “early” he teaches that it will come down even before its time.

For God, the steward of our affairs and the giver of spiritual gifts, knows, yes he knows, the time that suits his generous gifts to each person. But if someone proves good and upright, and compassionate and easy to guide besides, to him the rewards from God will be given early, so that they spring up in him like ears of grain. So too will his healing, that is, the casting off of every sickness and the entry of better things in its place.

For when someone is freed from the sicknesses of the soul, he will surely bear the fruit of longing and eagerness for every good thing whatever. So when the divine and spiritual light has dawned in us, healing surely rises with it in every way, as God dresses our wounds, saps the strength of our passions, and puts in their place within us the will to do good and to excel in righteousness.

That is why he says, “Your righteousness will go before you.” It will go before us, plainly, by making the road to godliness easy in advance, turning what is rough into what is smooth and passable, bringing down what is steep, and, as it were, setting straight our course toward all that is best.

He adds something else as well: “For the glory of God,” he says, “will wrap around you,” that is, it will surround you, make you someone all eyes turn to, and make you a benefit shared by many. For the brightness of the saints …

choices.why: PG prints αὐτοῦ with the marginal variant σοῦ; the second-person address requires the variant.
Cyril stresses the verb: the light bursts out like lightning, showing God's eagerness.
μοτόω, to apply lint to a wound.

choices.english: saps the strength of our passions
choices.why: ἀπονευρόω, to cut the sinews; God weakens the passions.
The glory makes the righteous conspicuous and a shared benefit.
